The Sincere, Sensitive, and Saccharinely Sweet Scion of the Chaturvedis is a voracious reader.
These are the two books he is shown reading in the movie.
answer_text: SALMAN KHAN IN HUM SAATH SAATH HAI

question_text:
The plot of the 2010 Hindi feature film, Udaan, kicks off when the protagonist, Rohan, and his three friends are expelled from their boarding school for sneaking off in the night. They do so to catch a screening of a semi-pornographic B-movie X, referred to as "Y ke X", perhaps to not confuse it with the X directed by 'another' master of his craft, and spare it the ignominy of the comparison.
ID the movie X, and its director, Y, who truly exemplifies the B in Bollywood.

What is the Bollywood connect of these two movies?
Toprak Ana (1973, Turkish)          Earth Crying (2002, Thai)
What is common between these Amitabh Bachchan movies?

Fahadh Faasil, popularly known as FaFa, made his debut as a nepo-baby in a 2002 movie, produced and directed by his filmmaker father. The film flopped, and so he quit acting and went to the US for his studies. While in the US, he comes across a DVD of a 2006 Hindi feature film, X, directed by an actor he admired, Y.
It is while watching this film that Fahadh rekindles his love for acting, sparked by a powerful performance by Irrfan Khan.
ID the film and the director that led to FaFa's discovery of Irrfan, and eventually to him returning to acting.
answer_text: Naseeruddin Shah; Yun Hota Toh Kya Hota

question_text: In the 2014 acclaimed Hindi feature film, X, one of the most intriguing elements of magical realism is hidden not in the dialogue or performances, but in the set design itself. The walls of the protagonist's house subtly but noticeably change colours as the narrative progresses, a creative choice symbolizing the passage of time and emotional shifts within the story. According to the director, the wall paint transitions through four distinct shades - beginning with blue, then turning yellow, then white, and finally returning to a different shade of blue - each representing a different season over the course of a year. ID the film X.

Parda hai Parda is a qawwali song featured in the Manmohan Desai film, Amar Akbar Anthony. The song was composed by Laxmikant-Pyarelal, while the lyrics were penned by Anand Bakshi. And while Mohammad Rafi sang most of the song, a single line in the song is sung by another singer, who is also duly credited in the album.
This is the portion of the song where the camera pans to Amitabh Bachchan in his character of Anthony Gonsalves, and he lip-syncs to the line "Akbar tera naam nahi".
Who is the other singer on this song?

X is a 2014 Hindi-language comedy film, starring Arshad Warsi in the role of a bumbling detective, and co-starring Soha Ali Khan, Javed Jaffrey, and Vijay Raaz.
The title of the film, same as the name of Arshad Warsi's character, is a name of Portuguese origin, and a play on the ever-readiness of the character to do each and every odd job that may come his way.
What is the title of this Arshad Warsi flick?

A subtle brand integration is always a tough task, especially when it comes to Bollywood. But Godrej pulls it off quite well, weaving their refrigerator brand into the story of this 2009 Bollywood film. In the movie, the leads are shopping in a supermarket, come across Godrej Eon Fridge, and the male lead convinces the female lead to enter a tagline writing contest to win a new fridge. Later in the film, Godrej Eon makes a reappearance as she wins the contest and a new fridge is delivered to her house.
ID the Bollywood film where this brand integration takes place.

In 1978, the director X was shooting two films simultaneously, and found a clever way of shooting one of his scenes twice - a separate take for each movie. In Jurmana with Amitabh Bachchan, the original scene appears as is - Amitabh playing a rich, spoilt brat, hitting on a woman in a restaurant. In the director's other film, Y, the same scene appears from behind-the-scenes in the form of an actual film shoot. As the film Y's protagonist walks in with his friend, his friend has a conversation with Amitabh where he even mentions the film's title as Jurmana.
ID the other film, Y, and its director, X.

In 2005, Sunny Deol starred in an Action-comedy film, X, that was met with widespread protests. Just as the film's promotions were taking momentum, with Sunny Deol's cry of "No if, no but… only Jatt" picking steam, sikh religious organizations protested against the film for using a sikh religious phrase as its title. Expecting trouble, the film put off from releasing in Punjab. Trouble still came around, as a couple of bomb blasts went off in New Delhi at theatres screening the film.
ID the title of this controversial release.

10ml Love is a 2012 Indian Hindi-language romantic comedy film directed by Sharat Katariya and starring Rajat Kapoor, Tisca Chopra, Purab Kohli, Koel Purie, Tara Sharma, and Neil Bhoopalam. The film's plot revolves around Rajat Kapoor's character finding a potion called Josh-e-Jawaani, and deciding to use it to make his wife (Tisca Chopra) fall in love with him again. Of course, the potion goes everywhere except where it was intended for.
Which Shakespearean play is the movie adapted from?

Either X did not know the time of Y's arrival or she couldn't care less. When Y rang the doorbell, X was busy deep-frying some stuff in besan - with her hands wrist-deep in the batter. With no servants around, she ran and opened the door herself. Tousled hair, hands in a mess, she used the back of her hand to push back a few strands of hair from her forehead, smearing some besan on to her hair.
Y never forgot this meet-cute, and immortalized it in the scene where the heroine is introduced in his 1973-teen romance.
Who are X and Y?

Aakhiri Mughal was supposed to be X's launch vehicle, to be directed by the same guy who eventually directed him in his debut. The story was a tale of Bahadur Shah Zafar's relationship with his son. However, the rights for the story were with another director, Kamal Amrohi, who once harboured ambitions to make the film with X's father, but that never materialized. And thus, neither father, nor son, could be a part of Aakhiri Mughal.
ID X.

X is a 2003 satirical dark-comedy film starring Arshad Warsi. The film is best known for featuring the song "Allah ke bande" sung by Kailash Kher. The film begins with the following disclaimer:
"This film is a mindless work of fiction. The characters happen to be fictional, despite our sincerest efforts. The locations, however, are real. The story has been plagiarized from several films."
The irreverent humour extends to the film's title as well.
ID this film.
answer_text: WAISA BHI HOTA HAI PART II

question_text:
TLV Prasad, son of noted Telegu filmmaker, T Prakash Rao, is a director in Hindi and Telegu films. This is a Limca Book of Records certificate he has for directing 29 films with the same lead actor between 1992 and 2002.
Ignoring the veracity of the said record, who is this lead actor?
